subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive client-scoped runs, or remain limited to background/clientless contexts?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix changes a shipped provider/model authorization boundary and existing operator trust semantics, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Widen The Existing Grant
options.body: Land the linked fix direction so one explicit plugin-scoped opt-in authorizes both interactive and background plugin subagent overrides, bounded by `allowedModels`.

options.title: Narrow The Scoped Contexts
options.body: Revise the fix to authorize only specific trusted backend or operator-scoped contexts while excluding plugin HTTP route or other external request scopes.

options.title: Keep Background-Only
options.body: Reject the behavior change and instead update SDK docs and runtime errors so operators know this config key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

recommendation.title: Widen The Existing Grant
recommendation.body: Land the linked fix direction so one explicit plugin-scoped opt-in authorizes both interactive and background plugin subagent overrides, bounded by `allowedModels`.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman introduced the trusted plugin subagent override policy and is the strongest feature-history owner for the config-contract decision.
